pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Saul and David — the young harper bent over his strings playing for the troubled king, for the choirmaster with stringed instruments a Maskil of David, listen to my prayer O God
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_saul_and_david

pictures.scene: Francisco de Zurbarán, Saint Francis in Meditation — the friar on his knees crying out with the skull held against him, and do not ignore my plea, attend to me and answer me
pictures.name: pd_zurbaran_saint_francis_in_meditation

pictures.scene: Vincent van Gogh, Sorrowing Old Man — the old man sitting by the fire with his fists pressed into his eyes, I am restless in my complaint, and distraught at the voice of the enemy
pictures.name: pd_van_gogh_sorrowing_old_man

pictures.scene: Honoré Daumier, The Uprising — the crowd surging up the street with one man's arm thrown into the air, at the pressure of the wicked, for they bring down disaster upon me
pictures.name: pd_daumier_the_uprising

pictures.scene: Hieronymus Bosch, Christ Carrying the Cross — the jeering faces crowded in on every side of Him, and resent me in their anger, my heart pounds within me
pictures.name: pd_bosch_christ_carrying_the_cross

pictures.scene: John Martin, Belshazzar's Feast — the whole hall turning in terror to the writing burning on the wall, and the terrors of death assail me, fear and trembling grip me
pictures.name: pd_martin_belshazzars_feast

pictures.scene: John Everett Millais, The Return of the Dove to the Ark — the dove brought in out of the flood and held close, and horror has overwhelmed me, I said oh that I had wings like a dove
pictures.name: pd_millais_the_return_of_the_dove_to_the_ark

pictures.scene: Adam Elsheimer, The Flight into Egypt — the family travelling away through the dark under the whole field of stars, I would fly away and find rest, how far away I would flee
pictures.name: pd_elsheimer_the_flight_into_egypt

pictures.scene: Ivan Kramskoi, Christ in the Wilderness — the solitary figure sitting on the stones of the desert at first light, in the wilderness I would remain, Selah
pictures.name: pd_kramskoi_christ_in_the_wilderness

pictures.scene: Ludolf Bakhuizen, Ships in Distress off a Rocky Coast — the vessels driven onto the rocks by the gale with nowhere to put in, I would hurry to my shelter, far from this raging tempest
pictures.name: pd_bakhuizen_ships_in_distress_off_a_rocky_coast

pictures.scene: Lucas van Valckenborch, The Tower of Babel — the builders still at work on the tower where the one language was broken, O Lord confuse and confound their speech, for I see violence and strife in the city
pictures.name: pd_valckenborch_the_tower_of_babel

pictures.scene: Peter Snayers, The Siege of Aire-sur-la-Lys — the army dug in all the way round the town in the snow, day and night they encircle the walls, while malice and trouble lie within
pictures.name: pd_snayers_the_siege_of_aire_sur_la_lys

pictures.scene: Hubert Robert, Fire at the Opera House — the burnt-out walls still smoking with the crowd working in the street below, destruction is within, oppression and deceit never leave the streets
pictures.name: pd_robert_fire_at_the_opera

pictures.scene: Paolo Uccello, The Battle of San Romano — the armed companies riding straight at each other with their lances down, for it is not an enemy who insults me, that I could endure
pictures.name: pd_uccello_the_battle_of_san_romano

pictures.scene: Joseph Wright of Derby, A Cavern near Naples — the great cave mouth opening onto the bay, a place to go out of sight, it is not a foe who rises against me, from him I could hide
pictures.name: pd_wright_of_derby_a_cavern_near_naples

pictures.scene: Giotto, The Kiss of Judas — the friend folding his cloak around Him and putting his face up to His, but it is you a man like myself, my companion and close friend
pictures.name: pd_giotto_the_kiss_of_judas

pictures.scene: Emanuel de Witte, Interior of a Church — two men walking in together under the arches, we shared sweet fellowship together, we walked with the crowd into the house of God
pictures.name: pd_de_witte_interior_of_a_church

pictures.scene: Nicolas Poussin, The Death of Sapphira — the woman dropping dead on the spot in front of the apostle, let death seize them by surprise, let them go down to Sheol alive
pictures.name: pd_poussin_the_death_of_sapphira

pictures.scene: Jan Steen, The World Turned Upside Down — the household drinking and dozing while everything goes to ruin around them, for evil is with them in their homes, but I call to God
pictures.name: pd_steen_the_world_turned_upside_down

pictures.scene: Gerrit Dou, Praying Old Woman — the old woman with her hands folded over the closed book, and the LORD saves me, morning noon and night I cry out in distress
pictures.name: pd_dou_praying_old_woman

pictures.scene: Eastman Johnson, The Lord Is My Shepherd — the man sitting alone by the hearth with the Bible open on his knee, and He hears my voice, He redeems my soul in peace
pictures.name: pd_johnson_the_lord_is_my_shepherd

pictures.scene: Jacques Courtois, Joshua Defeating the Amalekites — the horsemen packed together in the thick of the fighting, from the battle waged against me, even though many oppose me
pictures.name: pd_courtois_joshua_defeating_the_amalekites

pictures.scene: Guercino, God the Father — the Almighty above the clouds with both arms opened wide, God will hear and humiliate them, the One enthroned for the ages
pictures.name: pd_guercino_god_the_father

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, The Parable of the Rich Fool — the old man counting his money by candlelight with his books piled around him, Selah, because they do not change
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_the_parable_of_the_rich_fool

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, David and Uriah — the loyal officer walking out carrying the sealed order that will kill him, and they have no fear of God, my companion attacks his friends
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_david_and_uriah

pictures.scene: Govert Flinck, Isaac Blessing Jacob — the blind old father laying his hand on the son who has come in disguised, he violates his covenant, his speech is smooth as butter
pictures.name: pd_flinck_isaac_blessing_jacob

pictures.scene: Caravaggio, The Cardsharps — the accomplice signalling over the boy's shoulder while the cheat reaches for the hidden card, but war is in his heart, his words are softer than oil
pictures.name: pd_caravaggio_the_cardsharps

pictures.scene: Jacques-Louis David, The Oath of the Horatii — the three bare swords held up together in the father's fist, yet they are swords unsheathed, cast your burden upon the LORD
pictures.name: pd_david_the_oath_of_the_horatii

pictures.scene: Jacob van Ruisdael, Bentheim Castle — the castle standing on its rock above the woods, and He will sustain you, He will never let the righteous be shaken
pictures.name: pd_ruisdael_bentheim_castle

pictures.scene: John Martin, The Destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah — the fire coming down on the cities while the two who were warned get away over the ridge, but You O God will bring them down, to the Pit of destruction
pictures.name: pd_martin_sodom_and_gomorrah

pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, The Suicide of Saul — the king fallen on his own sword among the rocks as the armies close in, men of bloodshed and deceit, will not live out half their days
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_suicide_of_saul

pictures.scene: Ary Scheffer, Christus Consolator — the grieving and the bound gathered in close around the seated Christ, but I will trust in You
pictures.name: pd_scheffer_christus_consolator

lines.text: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. A Maskil of David.
Listen to my prayer, O God,
and do not ignore my plea.
Attend to me and answer me.
I am restless in my complaint,
and distraught at the voice of the enemy,
at the pressure of the wicked.
For they bring down disaster upon me
and resent me in their anger.
My heart pounds within me,
and the terrors of death assail me.
Fear and trembling grip me,
and horror has overwhelmed me.
I said, “Oh, that I had wings like a dove!
I would fly away and find rest.
How far away I would flee!
In the wilderness I would remain.
Selah
I would hurry to my shelter,
far from this raging tempest.”
O Lord, confuse and confound their speech,
for I see violence and strife in the city.
Day and night they encircle the walls,
while malice and trouble lie within.
Destruction is within;
oppression and deceit never leave the streets.
For it is not an enemy who insults me;
that I could endure.
It is not a foe who rises against me;
from him I could hide.
But it is you, a man like myself,
my companion and close friend.
We shared sweet fellowship together;
we walked with the crowd into the house of God.
Let death seize them by surprise;
let them go down to Sheol alive,
for evil is with them in their homes.
But I call to God,
and the LORD saves me.
Morning, noon, and night, I cry out in distress,
and He hears my voice.
He redeems my soul in peace
from the battle waged against me,
even though many oppose me.
God will hear and humiliate them—
the One enthroned for the ages—
Selah
because they do not change
and they have no fear of God.
My companion attacks his friends;
he violates his covenant.
His speech is smooth as butter,
but war is in his heart.
His words are softer than oil,
yet they are swords unsheathed.
Cast your burden upon the LORD
and He will sustain you;
He will never let the righteous be shaken.
But You, O God, will bring them down
to the Pit of destruction;
men of bloodshed and deceit
will not live out half their days.
But I will trust in You.
